key: Let not this fetter bind us fast: may he release us for success; For strong is Indra and renowned.
s: In a hymn to the Adityas and Aditi, pleading for life and release, the verse turns for once to Indra; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.56.8, reads the fetter as a net, and his preface to the hymn names fishes caught in one among its possible seers.

evidence.gloss: Let not the setu, the binding net, bind us; let him keep us clear, away from the net, for a great work. Who? Indra alone, renowned, the controller of all: let him keep us clear.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 8.56.8 at [675,8]); app 8.56 is standard 8.67, on which Sāyaṇa comments, and the Sanskrit labelled 8.56.8 (mā naḥ setuḥ siṣed ayam) is this verse. On the verse Sāyaṇa glosses setu as bandhako jālaḥ, the binding net, and Indra as the one who frees them from it: the reading holds. The fishes caught in a net, however, are not in his commentary on 8.56.8 but in his preface to the hymn (packet 8.56 introduction: बहवो वा मत्स्या जालनद्धाः सन्तो बन्धनमोक्षायादित्यानस्तुवन् । अतस्त एवर्षयः, restating the Anukramaṇī), so the sentence’s place was corrected: it now reads the fetter as a net at 8.56.8 and names the preface as where the fishes appear ("and his preface to the hymn names fishes caught in one among its possible seers"), and src now cites 8.56 and 8.56.8 (standard 8.67). Plain sense unchanged and faithful: Indra is named only in v8 of a hymn to the Adityas and Aditi asking for life and release. Revision year 2021 confirmed by the wiki API. Corrected entry passes entry-check.
